pahasapasaurus-gillettei:study:1.title: A new species of Pahasapasaurus (Plesiosauria: Polycotylidae) from the upper Cretaceous (lower Turonian) Tropic Shale of southern Utah, U.S.A. (Cretaceous Research, 2026)

facts.statement: Pahasapasaurus gillettei is a polycotylid plesiosaur species.
facts.quote: A polycotylid plesiosaur; a species of Pahasapasaurus.

facts.statement: The species was announced in 2025 and the final article will be published in 2026.
facts.quote: Announced in 2025, the final article version will be published in 2026.

facts.statement: Pahasapasaurus gillettei lived during the Late Cretaceous Turonian age.
The type locality of Pahasapasaurus gillettei is the Tropic Shale in Utah, United States.
The species was described by Schmeisser and McKean.
The genus Pahasapasaurus was established by Schumacher in 2007.
The genus is characterized by elongated epipodial bones and a distinctive palate bone structure.
facts.quote: Distinctive features of the taxon include elongate epipodial bones (radius/ulna - tibia/fibula) and the nature of the palate bones (roof of the mouth).

facts.statement: Pahasapasaurus lived in Late Cretaceous rocks of the United States.
facts.quote: Pahasapasaurus is an extinct genus of polycotylid plesiosaurs from Late Cretaceous rocks of the United States.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database currently has no record for Pahasapasaurus gillettei.
facts.quote: NOTE: PBDB has no record for Pahasapasaurus gillettei yet.

rejected.statement: Pahasapasaurus gillettei was named in 2025 based on a complete skull and partial skeleton from the early Turonian Tropic Shale of Utah.
rejected.quote: In 2025, a second species was named, Pahasapasaurus gillettei, based on a complete skull and partial skeleton from the early Turonian-aged Tropic Shale of Utah.
